newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee breaches 35.90-mark vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee breaches 35.90-mark vs dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee breached the 35.90-mark against the dollar on Thursday noon on aggressive dollar buying by a Calcutta-based bank, dealers said.
"It (dollar demand) began with local banks here," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "They they took over," he said, referring to the state-run bank that operates from Calcutta.
The rupee had opened the day at 35.88/90 per dollar.
The state-run bank and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have been the major dollar buyers in recent weeks.
Dealers said there were deals upto 35.9150 a dollar. This is the first time the dollar has breached the 35.90-mark in the new year. Spot dollar was quoted at 35.912/917 in latest deals.
